summary: Embedding ingest segment rotation caused ID misalignment and intermittent rerank timeouts for Cascadia Insights
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported intermittent rerank mismatches where top-k results returned text that did not match the corresponding embedding metadata, and requests experienced elevated tail latency and occasional timeouts. Impact: production traffic for Cascadia Insights search and recommendations degraded across two regions.

Impact:
- Incorrect rerank associations causing poor relevance for search and recommendations for a subset (~0.4%) of requests.
- Tail latency spikes and occasional 504s during background repair jobs.

Environment:
- Production ingestion pipeline with continuous delta uploads and periodic segment rotation/compaction enabled.
- Affected regions: us-west (primary), eu-central (replica).

Observed behavior:
- Reranker returned correct-looking embedding vectors but associated document text did not match expected IDs.
- Short windows (seconds-to-minutes) where topk ordering flipped and customers saw unrelated titles in results.
- During windows, system showed elevated I/O and index-sync jobs running and reranker queues grew, causing 504s for some long-tailed requests.

Expected behavior:
- Embedding vectors and metadata remain aligned for all queries. Segment rotation/compaction should be atomic and not expose transient misalignments.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Apply delta ingest payloads concurrently to the ingest API while a segment rotation is scheduled (we reproduced by forcing a rotation via admin endpoint).
2) Immediately query rerank endpoint for a set of recently-upserted IDs and observe topk document content vs expected metadata,
3) Observe increased reranker latency and occasional 504s during the same interval.

Cascadia (2026-03-10 17:05 UTC): Example request IDs: req_2391, req_2397, req_2412 around 2026-03-10T16:23-16:25Z. Attached a short recording of incorrect results.
SRE - Ravi (2026-03-10 17:18 UTC): Observed index sequence skew during a segment-rotation event. Kicked off forensic trace and snapshot of segment 8245. Marking as P1 Sev1.

investigation_notes: Timeline reconstruction showed segment rotation started at 2026-03-10T16:23:12Z while multiple upsert batches were concurrently flushing to the same segment. Rotation finalization code assumed flush quiescence; it did not acquire the compact lock atomically with delta commit, producing a transient ID offset by +1 for some entries.
Hypothesis: race between delta-commit seq advancement and segment-rotation atomic switch produced directory remapping where metadata->vector pointers were shifted for a small set of rows.

Reproduction: forced rotation + concurrent upserts reproduced identical misalignment locally in staging. Added stress test with 1000 concurrent small upserts and repeated rotations — reproduces within ~30s.

Telemetry: index-sync alerts and increased repair-job invocations during windows. Affected ~0.36% of queries hitting recently-upserted IDs in both regions. No data loss; vectors were intact, mapping was transiently misaligned.
Related artifacts: snapshot of segment 8245 uploaded to S3 (s3://redwood-debug/cascadia/seg-8245-20260310.tar.gz); heap traces and perf profiles attached in GitHub issue.
Root cause PR: concurrent finalization path did not hold the rotation lock across delta-commit; code path added in commit 3f8b2e7 (see PR #824).
resolution_summary: Patched ingest service to hold a rotation-finalize lock across delta commits and added a short quiesce window to guarantee pointer stability. Deployed patch v1.3.7 to affected clusters in us-west and eu-central. Backfilled mapping for affected segment 8245 and ran repair job to re-associate metadata pointers. Verified rerank correctness and tail latency returned to baseline. Notified customer and closed incident.
resolution_notes: Hotfix deployed: ingest v1.3.7 includes rotation lock + unit/integration tests to prevent regressions (PR #824 merged).
Backfill: executed mapping repair for segment 8245; repair job duration ~28s in us-west during a low-traffic window. No data loss observed.
Customer verification: Cascadia confirmed restored quality on 2026-03-11 morning.
Monitoring: added an alert rule that fires when index-seq-skew > 0 for more than 10s and created dashboard for segment-rotation metrics.
Follow-up tasks: INT ticket created to add CI stress test for rotation+concurrent-upserts (INT-402). Update runbook with safe-rotation checklist and required alerts.
